title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether the State-allocated Land Use Right of a Bankrupt Enterprise Should Be Included in the Bankruptcy Property and Other Issues

articles.content_en: 1. According to the provisions of Item (3), Paragraph 1, Article 58 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 47 of the Interim Regulations on the Assignment and Transfer of the Right to Use Urban State-Owned Land, the State-owned land-use rights obtained by a bankrupt enterprise by way of allocation shall not constitute bankruptcy property. When the enterprise goes bankrupt, the relevant people's government may recover such land-use rights and dispose of them according to law. With respect to State-owned enterprises included in the national merger and bankruptcy plan, the State-owned land-use rights lawfully obtained by them shall be handled pursuant to the relevant documents of the State Council.

2. An enterprise has no right to dispose of the State-owned land-use rights obtained by way of allocation. Where a mortgage is established on such land-use rights, the failure to obtain the approval of the people's government or the land administration department with examination and approval authority shall not affect the validity of the mortgage contract. Where the statutory approval procedures have been completed and mortgage registration has been made according to law, the mortgage shall be established upon registration. According to Article 51 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, a mortgagee may enjoy the right to preferential payment from the remaining portion only after the proceeds obtained from converting the mortgaged object into value, or from auction or sale, have been used to pay the amount equivalent to the land-use right assignment fee. However, with respect to State-owned enterprises included in the national merger and bankruptcy plan, where mortgages are established using State-owned land-use rights obtained by way of allocation, the matter shall be handled pursuant to the relevant documents of the State Council.

3. Where a State-owned enterprise establishes a mortgage on key equipment, complete sets of equipment, or buildings, if there are no other statutory circumstances rendering the mortgage void, the mortgage contract shall not be determined to be void merely on the ground that it has not been approved by the competent government department.
This Reply shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. This Reply shall apply to cases that are being tried or have not yet been tried, except for cases in which a retrial has been initiated against judgments or rulings that have already become legally effective.
This is hereby replied.
